during the period of the composition of

no creation x nhilo anywhere in the

x nihilo until around 170 CE and then it
develops after that and then you have
the development of the concept of
monotheism as we understand it today
beginning in the late 17th century CE
starting with the Cambridge platinist
Henry Moore around 1660 CE and what they
develop is a notion that builds on the
foundation of the notion that God
created absolutely all that exists apart
from God from nothing. So it requires
the doctrine that would not be created
till the late 2nd century CE. So you
cannot even have monotheism as we
understand it today anywhere in the
Bible. And you don't because the Bible
recognizes the existence of other gods
from beginning to end. And the reason
that people want to read monotheism into
the one god rhetoric of the Bible is
because they want their belief in
monotheism to be rooted in the Bible
because that's the inspired source of
their ideologies. And so in order to
maintain that ideological continuity
with the Bible, in order to be able to
say, "No, we got this from the Bible,
which is our inspired source for
everything," they have to be able to
find monotheism in the Bible. So you
have a lot of creative ways that
scholars have come up with for trying to
read monotheism into the Bible or trying
to revise what we understand monotheism
to be so that it can be identified in
the Bible. But monotheism is not in the
Bible. It is a post-biblical
philosophical innovation. And I recently
published an essay on monotheism in the

Religion. And I will have an essay
